title: Becca and the Fading Flame
markdown:
Dawn cracked. Brilliant light speared through the salt-frosted lighthouse windows. Becca the Lantern Witch’s eyes popped open. A peculiar quiet pressed down, prickling her skin. Her cozy room, usually buzzing with the mighty glow from her lantern, was dim. A flickering gloom pressed against the glass.

“Bother!” Her feet hit the cool stone with a thump. Something was wrong. The lighthouse lantern, the heart of her home, the beacon for every ship and creature, was failing. Becca’s own magic depended on its brilliance. If the lantern flickered, so did she.

She bolted and flung the door open. The lantern stood there, but its magnificent golden flame was a pathetic sputter, like a tired firefly ready to vanish. Her tummy did a wild flip-flop. “Oh, dear me, no!”

With the speed of a startled puffin she dashed down the spiralling stairs, sturdy boots clattering a frantic rhythm. At the bottom, where stone met the restless sea, stood Marble: a boy sculpted from smooth grey stone, eyes like polished pebbles holding ocean secrets.

“Marble!” Becca puffed, skidding to a halt. “My lantern! It’s gone dim! Utterly dim!”

Marble’s pebble eyes blinked. “I see it, Becca. The sea creatures are unsettled. Their songs are hushed. They feel the dimming light too. A weak light means a deep disturbance in the ocean’s heart.” His voice rumbled, soft and low, like pebbles on the shore. “The ancient tales speak of such times.”

“A disturbance? What kind?”

“The legend speaks of Piri, the magnificent pearl dragon. Her scales shimmer with captured dawn light. But her power, her essence, is bound to the sea’s ancient promises. And her light, like yours, is fading. Critically fading.”

Becca’s breath caught. A pearl dragon. Whispered tales only. “We have to find her! Before sunrise, Marble!”

Marble nodded, stone features etched with concern. “Sunrise is when the sea’s magic weakens. Its power recedes like the tide. If Piri’s light is faint, the sun could extinguish it. We must be swift.”

They hurried along the jagged shoreline, salty spray misting Becca’s cheeks. Ahead, a dark cavern gaped in the cliffs, guarded by colossal barnacle-covered boulders. This, Marble had said, was where the legend hinted Piri might be.

Blocking their path, coiled and immense, was a colossal grumpy Kraken, tentacles like thick writhing ropes covered in slime. Huge unsettling green eyes fixed upon them.

“Halt!” Its voice was deep thunder vibrating through the rocks. “None pass my watch! You wish to disturb the dragon? Answer my riddle, or face the deep! Listen closely: I stand tall, yet possess no legs. I guide countless travelers, but utter no sound. I shine with brilliant light, yet have no eyes to see. What am I?”

Becca’s quick mind whirred. She glanced at Marble, who gave a tiny nod. She looked back at the lighthouse, its feeble sputtering glow a desperate plea. Her lantern. “You are the lighthouse!”

The Kraken blinked. Tentacles drooped. “Blast and barnacles! You’ve bested me, witch-child. Fine. Pass. But tread carefully!”

Becca and Marble scurried into the damp cave. There, curled in a nest of shimmering seaweed, lay Piri. Breathtaking: scales a cascade of pearly colours, but the iridescence muted, dulled. Her breath puffed out in faint dying light.

“Piri,” Becca whispered. “We’ve come for your help. My lantern is failing. And we heard… perhaps you know why?”

Piri stirred, luminous eyes focusing. “My light dwindles,” she rasped, the mournful sigh of the tide. “The ancient promises… forgotten by the world above. The sea remembers, but the people have forgotten the magic.” A weak cough, a tiny spark fizzing feebly before vanishing. “If my light fades, child, your lantern will follow. The ships will sail into darkness.”

Sadness washed over Becca. She remembered a promise made years ago, as a tiny girl. She had found a struggling seahorse, fins caught. Carefully she had placed it back into the water, whispering, “I promise I will always protect the sea’s light.” She had never forgotten.

Then a bold thought sparked, hot and insistent. “Piri,” she said, stepping forward. “I have kept my promise. I tend this lighthouse with all my heart. And now I make you a new promise, a solemn vow. I promise to make your light shine again. Brighter than ever. I will ensure every sailor remembers this light, and the deep magic of the sea.”

As she spoke, a new shimmer appeared on Piri’s scales. The dragon’s eyes widened. Becca felt power surge through her, warm and vibrant. Even from here, the lighthouse lantern pulsed with its former glory.

“Your promise,” Piri breathed, voice stronger. “It burns with truth. It reignites the spark.”

With a magnificent rustle, Piri unfurled her wings. The cavern flooded with blinding light. The air thrummed. Ozone and sea salt. The dullness vanished, replaced by a radiant pulsing glow. Becca felt her own magic surge back, stronger, steadier.

They raced back to the lighthouse. As the first sunrays kissed the horizon, Becca’s lantern burst into a spectacular beam, a golden sword slicing through the mist. The sea creatures began their cheerful songs again. Marble smiled, pebble eyes twinkling.

Becca stood tall beside her blazing lantern. Dawn had work for her, and the lantern, at last, was ready to do it.
characters: Becca (a lantern witch), Marble (a statue boy), Piri (a pearl dragon)
